title: Specify lead reconciliation envelope
description: Validates the request and response envelopes of the agent-led lead-reconciliation step per RFC-29 §Lead reconciliation engine (D2). Discriminated by closed `kind`. `kind: request` is returned by `specrun plan propose --dry-run --format json`: a pure function of the parsed `discovery.md` carrying the lead catalog, deterministic required groups (exact id / exact alias / transitive cross-reference), advisory candidate blocks, unmatched leads, targets, and optional workspace projects. `kind: response` is the agent's grouping consumed by `specrun plan propose --from`: `lead-groups[]` partitions surveyed leads exactly once, while `slice-candidates[]` references those concepts and binds each `(concept-id, target)` pair to one target and optional project. The kernel validates this shape, enforces the global lead-partition and required-group invariants, derives unique `plan.yaml.slices[]` names from optional `slice-name` or concept/target fallback, and writes through the existing plan writers; it never auto-merges on its own heuristic. Closed top-level shape — unknown fields are rejected.

targetRef.description: Target adapter identifier, e.g. `omnia@v1` or `contracts@v1`. Mirrors `plan.schema.json` slice `target` pattern.

projectRef.description: One registered project from `registry.yaml`, surfaced into the request so the agent can bind each slice candidate to a project by matching the candidate's concept and target against the project's `target` and `description`. Mirrors `registry.yaml#/projects[]`.

name.description: Registry project name (`registry.yaml#/projects[].name`); the value the kernel writes to `plan.yaml.slices[].project` and that build-time workspace routing resolves against the registry.

target.description: The project's registered target adapter (`registry.yaml#/projects[].target`). A slice candidate may only bind to a project whose registered `target` equals the candidate's `target`.

description.description: Single-sentence domain characterisation (`registry.yaml#/projects[].description`). The disambiguation surface the agent judges against when more than one project shares a target.

matchBasis.description: How a lead joined its group. `exact-id` / `exact-alias` / `cross-reference` are deterministic kernel-computed matches; `semantic` is the agent's cross-source judgment and is surfaced for operator review.

requiredMatchBasis.description: Kernel-computed basis for a required group.

blockingKey.description: Deterministic key used only to build advisory candidate blocks, namespaced as `<kind>:<value>` (for example `domain:identity`, `module:auth`, `entity:user`, or `route:/password/reset`).

summary.description: One-line human-readable summary from the surveyed Lead.

aliases.description: Optional aliases from the surveyed Lead, used for exact-alias required groups and lexical fallback.

blocking-keys.description: Optional deterministic blocking keys emitted by source survey or derived by the kernel. Shared keys create advisory candidate-block edges; they are never semantic matches by themselves.

concept-id.description: Canonical concept id the required group is recorded under (the shared `id` for exact-id / cross-reference, the canonical id behind an alias for exact-alias).

block-id.description: Stable id for an advisory matching work queue. Response `lead-groups[].block-id` may cite it for review traceability.

keys.description: Blocking keys that caused the kernel to place these leads in one advisory block. Lexical fallback keys use the `token:<term>` namespace.

required-groups.description: Required-group concept ids included as possible extension anchors. The agent may extend such a group with open leads in the block but may not split the required group.

open-leads.description: Open leads to consider together for semantic matching within this advisory block.

required-groups.description: Deterministic exact-id / exact-alias / cross-reference groups the kernel pre-computed. The agent may extend a required group with semantic members but the kernel refuses any response that splits one.

candidate-blocks.description: Advisory matching work queues generated deterministically from blocking keys and lexical fallback. These reduce agent search space but do not constrain the final lead-groups[] response.

unmatched-leads.description: Open leads with no useful deterministic candidate block. The agent may leave them as single-lead groups or merge them semantically if it has a reason.

leads.description: Map of source-key to that source's surveyed leads, including summary and optional deterministic blocking metadata used to build candidate blocks.

projects.description: Registry topology in workspace mode — every entry from `registry.yaml#/projects[]` (name + target + description). Absent in single-repo mode (no `registry.yaml`, an empty registry, or a single-entry registry that behaves like single-repo mode); present and non-empty when the agent must bind each slice candidate to a project. The kernel computes this pre-pass from the parsed registry so the agent never re-reads `registry.yaml`.

tentative.description: Agent-flagged low-confidence membership; surfaced for operator review at Gate 1.

concept-id.description: Concept id for a unit of work. Slice candidates reference this id; it is not necessarily the derived plan slice name.

block-id.description: Optional id of the request candidate block that most directly explains this grouping. Review traceability only; the kernel does not constrain membership by block.

rationale.description: Agent's reason for the grouping; rendered into change.md for operator review, most useful on semantic merges.

concept-id.description: Concept id of a declared `lead-groups[]` entry. May repeat across slice candidates when the same concept fans out to multiple targets.

slice-name.description: Optional explicit plan slice name for this `(concept-id, target)` candidate. When omitted, the kernel derives a unique slice name deterministically.

target.description: Exactly one target per slice candidate (one slice per (concept, target) pair, per D5). The same concept may appear under more than one target.

depends-on.description: Derived slice names this candidate depends on (not concept ids). Each name must resolve to a projected `plan.yaml.slices[]` entry.

project.description: Registry project this slice candidate binds to, chosen by the agent from the request's `projects[]` by matching the concept and `target` against each project's `description` and registered `target`. Written verbatim to `plan.yaml.slices[].project` and resolved against `registry.yaml` by build-time workspace routing. Required on every candidate in workspace mode (request carried a non-empty `projects[]`); omitted in single-repo mode. The kernel rejects a value absent from `registry.yaml` (`plan-reconcile-project-orphan`) or whose registered target disagrees with the candidate's `target` (`plan-reconcile-project-target-mismatch`).

rationale.description: Agent's reason for target or project binding when the choice is not obvious; rendered into change.md for operator review.
